At 2:40 a.m., the scent of rising yeast always fought the smell of floor wax. Arthur wiped his flour-dusted hands on his apron and approached the wire cooling racks. There, resting between two wicker proofing baskets, sat a battered paperback copy of *The Count of Monte Cristo*. 

It was the fourth Thursday in a row. The first time, Arthur thought a customer had simply forgotten it. But every week, the exact same library book reappeared on the rack, always with its spine aligned perfectly with the edge of the metal shelf. 

Arthur picked it up. Tonight, a yellow sticky note clung to the cover. Written in elegant, shaky cursive, it read: *The baker in chapter five reminds me of you. Thank you for keeping the lights on.*

Arthur stared at the note, his thumb smoothing the creased paper. The bakery was silent save for the low hum of the refrigeration units. He didn't know who the late-night reader was, but he knew the book was due back at the municipal library down the street.

Arthur walked to the prep table, took a still-warm cinnamon roll, wrapped it carefully in parchment paper, and tucked it into his coat pocket to drop off at the library book return on his walk home.
